first.rationale: Current data shows simultaneous declines in activation (−6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (−4% QoQ), indicating a friction problem in the early funnel rather than pricing or messaging sensitivity. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that onboarding friction is directly remediable—field reduction drove SMB activation lift, and shortened onboarding improved completion and time-to-value. These are the highest-confidence, fastest-acting levers available. Verification of memory_31 and memory_86 will confirm effect sizes and cohort definitions before committing. While promotional_pricing addresses the competitive threat, it risks commoditization and margin erosion for a structural problem we can solve at the product layer. Referral_incentive requires an established-customer base in good health—our declining activation suggests we should stabilize the funnel first. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is secondary; it typically amplifies engagement but cannot overcome onboarding friction. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is high-value but orthogonal to the SMB-driven activation decline. A standard_experiment on simplified onboarding is the highest-probability path to recover qualified revenue sustainably: it directly addresses both reported metrics, leverages validated precedent, and positions us defensively against pricing pressure by improving perceived ease-of-use.
